definitions.explanation: Looking worn out, cheap, or in poor condition; giving an impression of poverty or neglect.

examples.japanese: みすぼらしい{服|ふく}を{着|き}ている。
みすぼらしい{建物|たてもの}が{並|なら}んでいる。
{昔|むかし}は{立派|りっぱ}だったが{今|いま}はみすぼらしくなった。
examples.english: It used to be splendid but has become shabby now.

notes:
みすぼらしい describes something that looks shabby, run-down, or poor. It conveys a visual impression of poverty or neglect.

FORMS:
- みすぼらしくない: not shabby (negative)
- みすぼらしく: shabbily (adverbial)
- みすぼらしかった: was shabby (past)
- みすぼらしさ: shabbiness (noun form)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- みすぼらしい{服|ふく}: shabby clothes
- みすぼらしい{建物|たてもの}: run-down building
- みすぼらしい{格好|かっこう}: shabby appearance
- みすぼらしくなる: to become shabby

WRITING:
Can be written as {見窄|みすぼ}らしい, but hiragana is standard.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {粗末|そまつ}: plain, humble, shabby (things, food)
- {貧相|ひんそう}: poor-looking (especially people's appearance)
- ボロボロ: tattered, falling apart (stronger, physical deterioration)
- {古臭|ふるくさ}い: old-fashioned, musty (emphasizes outdatedness)
